text:
sasha: Heads-up — started seeing 95th/99th tail blips on small-batch (1-4) generation in prod around 03:15 UTC, CPU-bound host stalls and sudden device memory pressure :thinking_face:
kai: Seen that too. Rough timeline from metrics: throughput steady, but p95 jumps +120ms for ~30s windows, repeat every ~10m.
sasha: I grabbed an nsys capture from a reproducer on staging (10 concurrent small requests). Putting notes here.
perfbot: nsys capture uploaded: https://perf.storage.company/trace/1945678901 (expires in 7d) :mag_right:
jordan: Quick observation from the timeline: large host->device memcpy spike right before the generic_attention kernel, followed by multiple small cudaMalloc calls interleaved. Looks like slab pool fragmentation + fallback to cudaMalloc for ~256B allocations.
lisa: That matches the KV cache eviction pattern we saw — repeated cache inserts on short-lived prompts causing new tensors and evictions. Evictions trigger async allocs that sometimes go direct to cudaMalloc.
kai: Does the kernel selector route small sequence lengths to the same kernel as long ones? I remember recent selector change to prefer fused kernels for throughput which might increase memory churn.
sasha: Yes — selector heuristic currently checks only token_count and batch_size, not kv_cache_hit_ratio or recent_alloc_rate. If fused path is chosen but backend wants a slightly different memory layout we do extra allocations.
jordan: Repro command I used:```bash
nsys profile -o smallbatch_spike --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --force-overwrite --sample=none --duration=30 --target-processes=all python run_repro.py --batch 2 --seq 64
```
sasha: nvprof snippet (from older capture) showing cudaMalloc spikes:```text
== PROFBOT ==
cudaMalloc 0x7ff..  0.12 ms
hostToDevice memcpy 0x7ff.. 1.3 ms
cudaMalloc 0x7ff..  0.11 ms
generic_attention.forward  8.4 ms
```
kai: Two quick hypotheses: 1) kernel selector picks a fused attention variant that requires temporary buffers not tracked by our pool; 2) pool fragmentation causes small allocs to fall back to cudaMalloc under contention.
lisa: I ran an experiment on staging toggling arena_compact_threshold down by 50% and saw the p95 drop ~40ms in the window where we used the same workload. Not fully deterministic but promising.
jordan: Can we make selector consider recent alloc failure rate? e.g., if pool_miss_rate > 2% in the last minute, favour the small-kernel path that uses preallocated buffers.
sasha: Agreed. Also adding quick KV heuristic: if kv_cache_insert_rate high, force non-fused path for batch<=4. Should reduce temporary buffer churn.
kai: I'll prototype a metric emitter for pool_miss_rate and add it to the routing policy. If it spikes, route to conservative kernel.
perfbot: Action created: PERF-873 add pool_miss_rate metric + selector fallback (assigned kai).
lisa: Also we should add an nsys capture with host allocations annotated: use NVTX scopes around pool alloc/evict calls so traces show them clearly. Example:```python
with nvtx.annotate("pool_alloc", color=0xFF0000):
    pool.alloc(size)
```
sasha: Good call. I'll add NVTX spans and re-run. If we confirm fragmentation, next step is to tune slab_size and slab_retention to reduce cross-request churn.
jordan: One more datapoint: testing quantized model reduces memory pressure and the spike disappears — supports allocator fallback theory rather than pure kernel perf.
kai: Plan: 1) add NVTX spans + pool_miss_rate metric, 2) run paired nsys captures (default vs selector-with-fallback) on staging, 3) tune slab params and roll a canary. I'll post results here. :rocket:
sasha: Thanks — if anyone has an easy reproducer script ping me, I'll attach to the ticket.
lisa: I pushed a tiny perf test to staging branch 'perf/1945-kv-alloc-spike' with NVTX and a sample driver. Use `make repro-staging` to run.
kai: Running it now, will share traces shortly. :eyes:
